# Josie Pye

## Overview

- **Gender:** female  <sub>[v1 c35 P6](../source/v01-c35.md#nw-v01-c35-p0006)</sub>
- **Origin:** Avonlea  <sub>[v1 c38 P40](../source/v01-c38.md#nw-v01-c38-p0040), [v3 c16 P2](../source/v03-c16.md#nw-v03-c16-p0002)</sub>

## Appearance

Josie is a fat girl. She was once described as looking like a red-haired fairy.

_Sources: [v1 c24 P14](../source/v01-c24.md#nw-v01-c24-p0014)_

## Personality

Josie is disagreeable, sharp-tongued, sulky, and malicious. She tends to be envious and triumph over others when victorious. She can be quite rude and holds grudges against her peers.

_Sources: [v1 c23 P6](../source/v01-c23.md#nw-v01-c23-p0006), [v1 c24 P14](../source/v01-c24.md#nw-v01-c24-p0014), [v1 c35 P6](../source/v01-c35.md#nw-v01-c35-p0006), [v1 c37 P33](../source/v01-c37.md#nw-v01-c37-p0033), [v3 c11 P41](../source/v03-c11.md#nw-v03-c11-p0041), [v3 c16 P2](../source/v03-c16.md#nw-v03-c16-p0002)_

- disagreeable  <sub>[v1 c37 P33](../source/v01-c37.md#nw-v01-c37-p0033)</sub>

## Abilities

- walking board fences  <sub>[v1 c23 P6](../source/v01-c23.md#nw-v01-c23-p0006)</sub>

## Goals

- going to college for education's sake  <sub>[v1 c30 P21](../source/v01-c30.md#nw-v01-c30-p0021)</sub>

## History

During spelling class at Avonlea school, Josie cheated by looking in her book to get ahead, but got flustered when Anne Shirley caught her. During a outdoor gathering, Josie dared Jane Andrews to hop around the garden on one leg. When Jane failed, Josie celebrated her victory and was challenged in turn by Anne to walk along the top of the Barrys' board fence, which Josie accomplished with ease. When preparing for a concert, Josie became sulky because she wanted to play the fairy queen, a role given to Jane Andrews instead. Following the concert, she did not speak to Julia Bell for three months after commenting that Julia's bow resembled a chicken jerking its head. Upon seeing Anne's newly clipped hair, Josie remarked that she looked like a scarecrow. At the Exhibition, Josie earned first prize for her knitted lace. When studying for Queen's Academy Entrance exams, she reminded Anne that the number thirteen was unlucky. Later, while attending Queen's Academy, she earned a reputation as the sharpest-tongued student present. Unlike many of her classmates, she stated she planned to go to college for education's sake rather than out of necessity to earn a living. Later, when Anne's prize-winning story was published, Josie spitefully claimed Anne had merely copied it from an old paper.

_Sources: [v1 c15 P25](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0025), [v1 c23 P5](../source/v01-c23.md#nw-v01-c23-p0005), [v1 c23 P6](../source/v01-c23.md#nw-v01-c23-p0006), [v1 c24 P14](../source/v01-c24.md#nw-v01-c24-p0014), [v1 c26 P2](../source/v01-c26.md#nw-v01-c26-p0002), [v1 c27 P40](../source/v01-c27.md#nw-v01-c27-p0040), [v1 c29 P24](../source/v01-c29.md#nw-v01-c29-p0024), [v1 c30 P21](../source/v01-c30.md#nw-v01-c30-p0021), [v1 c32 P7](../source/v01-c32.md#nw-v01-c32-p0007), [v1 c35 P6](../source/v01-c35.md#nw-v01-c35-p0006), [v3 c2 P3](../source/v03-c02.md#nw-v03-c02-p0003), [v3 c16 P2](../source/v03-c16.md#nw-v03-c16-p0002)_
